fallback.what: Two distinct fallbacks remain, both keyed by agentKey / policyId — never by role: (1) constant fallback (resolveConstantPolicySource path): when the resolved policy row is missing, an agent whose agentKey maps to a built-in name (vteam-<agentKey> in ROLE_BOUNDARIES) resolves the constant-derived policy (resolveBuiltinPolicy); (2) agentKey-derived policyId path: when policyId is null but agentKey is a built-in name, policyKeyOf resolves the conventional id ep_<agentKey> and reads the existing DB row (which may carry user edits).
fallback.why: The migration backfilling policyId is todo 7; until it lands, existing installs have built-in agents with policy_id NULL. If policyKeyOf returned null unconditionally, resolveByAgent would skip existing (possibly user-edited) built-in policy rows and silently revert every such agent to factory constants — a capability change, not a refactor. The retained path is NOT the old ep_<role> derivation: it is derived from agentKey, so a row without agentKey no longer fabricates a policy id, and role is never consulted.
fallback.decision: KEEP a policyId-keyed path, derived from agentKey only. The ep_<role> string derivation is removed. Natural removal point: after todo 7 backfills policy_id, the fallback branch becomes dead and can be deleted by todo 8.
fallback.degradationWhenNeither: agentKey absent and policyId null -> policyKeyOf returns null -> constantRoleNameOf(undefined) returns null -> resolveAgentWithFallback returns null (no throw), identical to today's behaviour for an unknown/no-role agent.
